rules.title: San Francisco Just Cause Eviction Requirement (Rent Ordinance Section 37.9(a))
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance only for one of 17 enumerated just causes, which must be the dominant motive for the eviction. Expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership alone is not just cause.

needs_facts: rental unit covered by Rent Ordinance

rules.coverage_text: Rental units covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance, including some units exempt from the rent increase limits (e.g., units with a certificate of occupancy after June 13, 1979, Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies, some government-regulated tenancies).
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.
rules.penalty: Landlord who evicts or tries to evict unlawfully may be subject to substantial civil and/or criminal liability.

rules.title: Just cause required to remove housing services
rules.requirement: A landlord needs a just cause reason to take away or remove access to certain housing services such as garage, parking, storage, and laundry rooms. Landlords who comply with Section 37.2(r) may temporarily remove services such as parking and storage to perform mandatory soft-story seismic retrofit work.

needs_facts: rental unit covered by Rent Ordinance

rules.coverage_text: Housing services in units covered by the Rent Ordinance.
rules.exemptions_text: Temporary removal of services (e.g., parking and storage) allowed for mandatory soft-story seismic retrofit work if landlord complies with Section 37.2(r).
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord also needs a "just cause“ reason to take away or remove access to certain
housing services
, including but not limited to garage facilities, parking facilities, driveways, storage spaces, and laundry rooms.

rules.title: Just cause applies to some units exempt from rent increase limits
rules.requirement: Tenancies exempt from the Ordinance's rent increase limits, including units with a first Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies, and some government-regulated tenancies, remain subject to just cause eviction rules.
rules.coverage_text: Newly constructed units with first Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies, and some tenancies regulated by another agency.
rules.quoted_span: Some tenancies that are exempt from the rent increase limitations of the Ordinance are still subject to the eviction provisions of the Ordinance, and tenants in these categories can only be evicted for one of the “just cause” reasons listed in the Ordinance.
